title: Нагиев присоединяется к ужину  (Nagiyev Joins the Late Dinner)

segments.t: Just as Chef Barinov is about to lose his temper at Vika and her waitresses for tricking the kitchen into cooking their staff dinner, Nagiyev strolls into the dining room. Forced to smile and play along, Viktor Petrovich watches helplessly as Nagiyev sits down and orders another salad.
А что это мы хомячим, а?
Надеюсь, не за мой счет, а?
Ладно, давайте мне тоже вот там бы накрыть.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Let me call you back in a minute.' Leaning in quietly with Kostya, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Where did I just walk in, a zoo?' Kostya questions openly if there is more going on behind the scenes.
А что это мы хомячим, а?
'And what are we all munching on here, huh?' Max chimes in promptly in front of Kostya and puts the weight on "khomyachim" ("to munch, snack on", from "khomyachit") as the exchange unfolds.
Надеюсь, не за мой счет, а?
'Not on my tab, I hope, huh?' Focusing on the account with Max, Kostya keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Max purely through rising pitch.
'No, no, of course not.' Max counters honestly watching Kostya, watching Kostya's face to see how the news lands.
Ладно, давайте мне тоже вот там бы накрыть.
'Alright, go ahead and set a place for me over there too.' Kostya proceeds evenly in the exchange and lands on "davayte" ("let's", built on "davat") to keep the statement grounded.
'I would gladly eat something myself.' Max pushes back decisively in the exchange and lands on "syel" ("ate", built on "syest") to keep the statement grounded.
'Yes, right away.' Kostya firmly extends this direct affirmation while facing Max using "da" ("yes") — a crisp "da" ("yes") that confirms the point without extra words.
'Stop nodding like that.' Max speaks dryly before Kostya and puts the weight on "kivayte" ("to nod", from "kivat") as the exchange unfolds.
'Take the order.' Focusing on the order in front of Max, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'What is this, they want seconds now?' Max asks straight out while looking straight at Kostya here.
'One more salad.' Mentioning the salad around Max, Kostya puts the emphasis on "salat" ("salad") in the middle of the talk.
'You will get your salad.' Cutting in firmly during the talk, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
А что это мы хомячим, а?
Надеюсь, не за мой счет, а?
Ладно, давайте мне тоже вот там бы накрыть.
That wraps up this scene as before Chef Barinov can explode at Vika and the waitresses, Nagiyev walks in and asks to join their late meal, ordering one more salad from the kitchen. Until next time!
